framework.name: Observable Behaviors of Entrepreneurial Mindset
framework.publisher: Engineering Unleashed / ASEE NEMO research lineage
framework.licenseNotes: Canonical names and definitions should be confirmed against A Field Guide for EM Behaviors before public distribution. This prototype seeds the eight behaviors from a Field Guide extract used for faculty UX testing; it is not a substitute for the published source.
framework.provenance: Seeded from the Field Guide extract in a related EM Behaviors project (field-guide.js). Replace or confirm against the official Field Guide PDF when it is added to this repository. Habit–behavior relationships are not encoded; faculty select independently.

items.name: Adapts to Change
items.definition: Adjusts plans and designs when constraints, regulations, or stakeholder priorities shift.
examples: Redesigns a polymer when regulations change rather than abandoning the project or fighting the rule.

items.name: Asks Discerning Questions
items.definition: Asks discerning, open-ended questions before offering solutions—especially when a quick fix or familiar approach is already on the table.
examples: When a team jumps to gamification for an app engagement problem, an EM-minded engineer first asks what users experience today and what blocks deeper engagement.

items.name: Communicates Value Propositions
items.definition: Tailors how value is communicated to what each audience cares about most.
examples: Presents the same prosthetic innovation differently to patients, insurers, and clinicians.

items.name: Learns from Failure
items.definition: Treats failure as a source of learning data rather than as evidence of personal inadequacy or reason to abandon a worthy goal.
examples: After repeated prototype safety failures, reframes each outcome as information about requirements rather than as a verdict on ability.

items.name: Identifies Value Opportunities
items.definition: Notices problems and friction points that may signal broader opportunities to create value.
examples: When software crashes under certain loads, investigates whether others share the problem—a possible product gap.

items.name: Gathers Supporting/Refuting Data
items.definition: Seeks evidence that both supports and challenges an idea before committing to a course of action.
examples: Before recommending green roofs for heat-island mitigation, gathers studies showing benefits and limitations.

items.name: Identifies Stakeholder Impact
items.definition: Considers how a solution affects multiple stakeholder groups, including indirect and potentially negative impacts.
examples: Evaluates an automated parking system for drivers, planners, businesses, and enforcement—not only end users.

items.name: Integrates Information
items.definition: Synthesizes technical, human, regulatory, and economic inputs into coherent decisions.
examples: Designs healthcare app architecture that simultaneously addresses HIPAA, UX, clinical workflow, and security.
